name: Losar (Tibetan New Year)
description: Three-day Tibetan New Year celebration marking the Fire Horse Year (2026). Families prepare khapse (traditional Tibetan sweets), monasteries conduct prayers, and thousands gather at Tsuglagkhang temple. Dalai Lama participates in celebrations.
significance: Major religious and cultural festival for the Tibetan exile community in McLeod Ganj, central to Buddhist practice and annual renewal.

name: Dalai Lama's Birthday
description: Celebration of His Holiness the Dalai Lama's birthday, featuring prayers and cultural events at Tsuglagkhang temple and surrounding areas. Monastics from all traditions, dignitaries, and Buddhist practitioners gather for ceremonies.
significance: Significant religious observance for the Tibetan Buddhist community, marking the 90th birthday (2026) with special significance.

name: Manimahesh Yatra
approximate_date: August 16 - September 19 (Janmashtami to Radha Ashtami, lunar calendar)
description: Sacred pilgrimage to Manimahesh Lake (4,080m) at the foot of Mount Kailash in Bharmour region, coinciding with Krishna Janmashtami. Thousands of devotees trek to the holy lake. Bharmour hosts a fair with local customs and rituals.
significance: One of the major Hindu pilgrimages in Himachal Pradesh, held on the sacred lunar calendar tied to Krishna's birth, attracting devotees region-wide.

name: Shrikhand Mahadev Yatra
description: Sacred pilgrimage to Shrikhand Mahadev peak (18,570m) featuring a naturally formed 75-foot Shivling. One of the most challenging treks in India, organized by Kullu District Administration during the Shravan month (auspicious for Shiva worship). Base camps with facilities at five locations.
significance: Panch Kailash shrine, considered one of the toughest pilgrimages in India. Shravan is the most sacred month for Shiva worship in Hindu tradition.

name: Kinner Kailash Parikrama
description: 60 km sacred pilgrimage circuit around Kinner Kailash peak in Kinnaur, with a naturally formed 79-foot Shivling at 4,400m. Trek starts from Charang village and ends at Chitkul in Baspa Valley. Believed to grant spiritual liberation through karmic purification.
significance: Sacred circumambulation (parikrama) of the peak believed to be Lord Shiva's divine dwelling place. Central to regional Hindu spirituality.

name: Phulaich (Festival of Flowers)
description: Festival celebrating wildflower blooms in upper Kinnaur, featuring processions of local deities, traditional folk dances, and reenactments of ancient war scenes in traditional attire. Three-day 'Ukhyang' celebration at Sangla Valley organized by Kinnaur administration.
significance: Tribal harvest festival of the Kinnaura people, celebrating the bond between community and nature. Central to local cultural identity.

name: Prashar Mela (Parashar Fair)
description: Annual fair at the 13th-century Parashar Rishi Temple on the shores of Prashar Lake (2,730m) in Mandi district. Devta processions where idols of regional deities are carried in traditional sedans by foot. Includes folk music and local cuisine.
significance: Regional pilgrimage fair dedicated to Sage Parashar, attracting devotees from neighboring valleys. Important cultural gathering for mountain communities.

name: Minjar Fair
description: Major Chamba district fair held at Chaugan ground celebrating the harvest season. Farming community offers first corn silk ('Minjar') to River Ravi for good harvests. Features stalls selling local crafts and produce, with evening cultural performances.
significance: Agricultural festival central to farming communities in Chamba, held across the region including Dalhousie area, representing gratitude for nature's bounty.

name: Losar (Tibetan New Year / Halda)
description: Buddhist new year celebration in Lahaul known locally as 'Halda', marking the end of harvest season. Monasteries perform ritual 'Cham dances' (masked devil dances) in colorful costumes depicting triumph of good over evil. Includes traditional Tibetan Buddhist ceremonies.
significance: Sacred renewal festival for Buddhist communities in the high Himalayan valleys, central to regional spiritual practice.

name: Kullu Dussehra
description: Major regional festival celebrated in Parvati Valley including Kasol and Manikaran areas. Features pilgrimage activities, prayers and rituals to Lord Shiva (Triloknath/Avolokiteshvara), folk dances, temple processions, and mini fairs with music performances and traditional Himachali cuisine.
significance: Major Hindu festival across the region, combining spiritual worship with community celebration and cultural expression.

name: Regional Spiti Buddhist Festivals
description: While no direct celebrations occur at Chandratal Lake itself, the surrounding Spiti Valley celebrates Buddhist festivals including pilgrimages to Triloknath (Shiva as Lord of Three Worlds), with folk dances, temple processions, and lama rituals. Losar (Tibetan New Year in February) is also celebrated regionally.
significance: Buddhist cultural observance in the high Spiti Valley region, connecting remote Himalayan communities to broader Tibetan Buddhist tradition.

name: Kullu Dussehra
description: Regional festival celebrated in communities surrounding Great Himalayan National Park in Kullu district. Major Hindu festival with spiritual significance throughout the park area.
significance: Regional celebration connecting mountain communities, central to local cultural calendar.

name: Fagli Festival
approximate_date: March (Amavasya/moonless night, aligned with Basant Panchami)
description: Traditional tribal festival in Yangpa village and Tirthan Valley marking the end of winter and victory of good over evil. Men in traditional masks dance in circles while locals gather. Arrow shooting at Ravana portraits occurs in some villages during Basant Panchami.
significance: Ancient tribal celebration of seasonal transition and spiritual purification unique to Kinnaur district communities.

name: Tribal Festival (Janjatiya Utsav)
description: State-level tribal festival celebrated at Reckong Peo (district headquarters) annually since 1987 (earlier known as Janjatiya Utsav and Phulaich Utsav). Showcases panorama of Kinnaur's rich cultural heritage with exhibitions of horticulture/agriculture produce, handicrafts, and artifacts. Celebration of tribal traditions and local knowledge.
significance: Official state-level tribal celebration showcasing Kinnaur's unique cultural identity and providing economic opportunity for local artisans and farmers.
